Looking at the immune layer code with fresh eyes, focusing on what prior rounds missed. Applying P-pass to each candidate before inclusion.

FINDING_ID: CC_IM_F001
SEVERITY: 0.82
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.65
DESCRIPTION: `self_diagnose()` Self-check 3 (chain exhaustion rate) emits a CRITICAL diagnosis but never updates `self._last_self_adjust_round[_trigger_key_3]`. Self-checks 1 and 2 both record `self._last_self_adjust_round[_trigger_key] = current_round` after acting, but Self-check 3 only appends a diagnosis and returns. Since `_last_3` stays at `-999`, the damping gate `current_round - _last_3 >= damping_rounds` is permanently satisfied. Once `chain_exhaustion_rate > 0.5` and `len(self._chain_exhaustion_history) >= 2`, a CRITICAL diagnosis is emitted every single round for the remainder of the run, flooding `_diagnoses` and inflating the denominator of `false_positive_rate`.
PROPOSED_FIX: Add `self._last_self_adjust_round[_trigger_key_3] = current_round` immediately after appending the diagnosis inside the `exhaust_rate > 0.5` block — matching the pattern used by Self-checks 1 and 2.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: CC_IM_F002
SEVERITY: 0.78
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.72
DESCRIPTION: All per-model directive transforms (`add_synthesis_directive`, `add_parsing_directive`, `add_verification_directive`) use set-if-absent semantics: `if model.model_id not in self.config.per_model_directives`. Once any remediation chain places a directive on a model, every other directive-based transform for that model permanently returns `None`. Consequence chain: (1) `parser_yield` chain step 0 adds a parsing directive to model X. (2) Later, `findings_decline` chain step 0 (`add_synthesis_directive`) skips model X because it already has a directive. If all models already have directives, `_apply_transform` returns `None`. (3) When `_apply_transform` returns `None`, `apply_diagnosis` does not call `set_remediation_state`. (4) Without remediation state, the FFF-D suppression gate in `record_round` (`"findings_decline" not in self._remediation_state`) stays open. (5) Next round, the diagnosis fires again, `apply_diagnosis` tries the same step, gets `None` again — indefinitely. This also means a model can never receive both a parsing directive AND a synthesis directive, even though both may be needed simultaneously.
PROPOSED_FIX: Change directive transforms to append to existing directives (with a separator and length check) instead of set-if-absent: `current = self.config.per_model_directives.get(model_id, ""); new = (current + "\n" + directive).strip(); if len(new) <= self.config.max_per_model_directive_chars: ...`. Also, when `_apply_transform` returns `None`, `apply_diagnosis` should still set remediation state (marking the step as attempted) so the suppression gate and outcome verification can function.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: CC_IM_F003
SEVERITY: 0.77
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.74
DESCRIPTION: When P-pass rejects a remediation step, `apply_diagnosis` escalates by incrementing `chain_idx` but does NOT reset `applied_round` or `metric_at_apply` in the existing `_remediation_state` entry. Code path: `if state: state["chain_idx"] = chain_idx + 1` — only `chain_idx` is updated. In `_verify_remediation_outcomes`, `rounds_since = current_round - state["applied_round"]` uses the stale `applied_round` from whenever the PREVIOUS step was applied. If enough rounds have elapsed, verification immediately fires for a step that was never applied. It then evaluates whether the metric improved — but nothing was done. If the metric happened to improve naturally, the system logs "Remediation SUCCESSFUL" for an unapplied step and clears the pathology. If not, it escalates further or exhausts the chain, all based on evaluation of a phantom fix.
PROPOSED_FIX: In the `if not proceed` block of `apply_diagnosis`, update `applied_round` and `metric_at_apply` when escalating: `state["applied_round"] = round_idx; state["metric_at_apply"] = current_metric_val`. This ensures the verification window starts from the escalation point. Also add `"chain_length"` to the seeded state in the `else` branch (partially noted in ChatGPT_IM_F004, but `applied_round`/`metric_at_apply` staleness was not).
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: CC_IM_F004
SEVERITY: 0.72
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.68
DESCRIPTION: `record_dispatch_success_after_block()` is defined on `DynamicManager` but never called anywhere in the shown codebase. `process_round()` does not track which models succeeded after being blocked in a prior round. `_dispatch_successes_after_block` therefore remains permanently empty for all models. In `check_dispatch_health()`, the dispatch false-positive check `if any(s > block_round for s in successes)` always evaluates to `False` because `successes` is always `[]`. This makes the entire dispatch false-positive detection path dead — not from logic bugs in the detection code itself, but because the necessary input events are never recorded. The chain `dispatch_false_positive` in `_REMEDIATION_CHAINS` and the legacy hardcoded branch in `apply_diagnosis` are both unreachable.
PROPOSED_FIX: In `process_round()`, after failure detection succeeds for a model (failure_type is None), check whether that model has any prior entries in `self._dispatch_blocks[mid]`. If so, call `self.record_dispatch_success_after_block(mid, round_idx)`. This wires the success-after-block event into the processing pipeline.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: CC_IM_F005
SEVERITY: 0.70
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.60
DESCRIPTION: `_sensitivity_decay` is a single scalar shared across all detectors, but Self-check 2 modifies it based on the aggregate `false_positive_rate` across all pathology types. The `effective_window()` function in `record_round()` uses `self._sensitivity_decay` for every detector: `widen = decay ** (-resolved)`. If mu detection has a high false-positive rate but kappa detection does not, Self-check 2 increases `_sensitivity_decay` from 0.8 toward 0.95. This widens the effective detection window for ALL detectors (kappa, mu, findings_decline, vocab_saturation) — including those with zero false positives. A genuine kappa pathology that was correctly detected at window=3 might now require window=5 to trigger, delaying detection by 2 rounds because an unrelated detector was over-sensitive.
PROPOSED_FIX: Make `_sensitivity_decay` per-detector: `Dict[str, float]` keyed by detector name (kappa, mu, etc.), with Self-check 2 adjusting only the detectors that contributed to the elevated false-positive rate. Requires tracking which detectors produced the natural resolutions counted in `false_positive_rate`.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: CC_IM_F006
SEVERITY: 0.67
FLAW_CLASS: 4
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.55
DESCRIPTION: `record_model_round()` has no resolution path for `model_failure_{model_id}`. When a model recovers (`failed=False`), `_model_failure_counts[model_id]` is reset to 0, preventing new diagnoses. But `_pathology_counts[f"model_failure_{model_id}"]` is never cleared, `_resolved_counts` is never incremented, and `record_natural_resolution` is never called. ChatGPT_IM_F006 and F007 identified this for `parser_yield` and `cpf_spike`; the identical gap exists for `model_failure`. When the model next fails (consecutive >= 2 again), persistence resumes from the accumulated count, immediately escalating to CRITICAL severity regardless of how many rounds of healthy operation intervened. The elevated persistence also inflates the `effective_window` narrowing via `_sensitivity_growth`, making the monitor increasingly hair-trigger for a model that experienced failures early in the run but has since recovered.
PROPOSED_FIX: Add a resolution branch in `record_model_round()` for `model_failure_{model_id}`: when `not failed` and `_pathology_counts.get(key, 0) > 0`, use the resolution-counter + hysteresis pattern (matching monotonic_decline's existing resolution path). On resolution, call `record_natural_resolution(key)` and clear `_pathology_counts[key]`.
VERIFIED: TRUE
